titel: Should there be an age group finish tape at pro races, triathlon training euphoria, and more!

faehigkeiten.grund: Dynamik weder belegt noch ausgeschlossen: keine Merkmale gefunden, aber eine unveraenderte Wiederholungsprobe beweist nichts

einzeiler: Pro triathletes discuss race finish tapes, training euphoria, and run forms.
kurzfassung: The hosts share updates on injury recovery and upcoming travel before answering listener questions. Topics include whether age groupers deserve finish tapes, finding euphoria in training, and managing luggage fees. They also discuss transitioning to pro, open water swim training, and traveling to Chattanooga.
stichpunkte: Eric shares a positive hip recovery update after a recent trail run.
The hosts dive into an airline-themed rapid fire ahead of traveling to Nice.
A listener asks whether age groupers should get a finish line tape at races with pros.
Discussion on whether triathlon training produces a feeling of euphoria similar to skateboarding.
The hosts discuss running form cues, cadence, and avoiding overthinking strides.
Sharing extreme airport luggage fee stories and travel strategies for bikes.
Advice on when new pros should consult lawyers for contracts and where to base themselves.
Tips on open water swimming, handling pre-race physical slumps, and visiting Chattanooga.

clips.hook: Hopeless to hopeful on the trails
clips.text: The speaker expresses profound relief after experiencing a month of despair regarding a severe physical setback.

clips.hook: Over 30,000 views in under a day
clips.text: The hosts marvel at the surprisingly rapid online traction and massive audience enthusiasm for their latest video release.
A staggering airport baggage charge shared on another show sparks astonishment among the hosts.

clips.hook: Do you need a lawyer when turning pro?
clips.text: The reality of early career sponsorships is addressed, noting that fresh pros lack the leverage to demand complex legal negotiations.

clips.hook: Meltdowns at the happiest place on earth
clips.text: A humorous observation highlights the irony of children crying during an expensive and supposedly magical vacation.

beschreibung:
Nick is recording from his neighbor's WiFi, Eric's in the van, Paula is doing her own audio engineering, but the gang got it together anyway! We kick things off with an airline Rapid Fire before getting into a full question bag that covers racing, going pro, travel logistics, and a Chattanooga guide for a UK family about to combine 70.3 Worlds with Disney World.
This week we discussed:
Airline rapid fire: favorite snack, drink, seat, airline, and Paula's method for dealing with an overweight bag at the counter
Should there be a separate finish line tape for the top age grouper at Ironman races with a pro field?
Is there anything in triathlon that matches the euphoria of finally landing a skateboarding trick?
Run form analysis: when to think about it, when to leave it alone, Paula's mirror trick on the Kickr Run, and why fixing one thing can break something else up the chain
Airline luggage horror stories — Eric's €550 Lufthansa bill and why United loyalty is a financial decision
Turning pro: do you actually need a lawyer, contract clauses worth paying attention to, and where to train when you make the jump
Open water vs. pool for easy swims in summer, is it even a question?
Feeling flat, disconnected, and off 17 days out from Ironman Wisconsin, what's actually happening and what to do about it
Chattanooga as a destination for a UK family combining 70.3 Worlds with Disney World: the honest guide, how many days at Disney is too many, and what to actually expect from the city
